title: Your Name Is on the Label—Do You Own It?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A founder's name on a label signals identity and reputation; it does not, by itself, answer who owns the registered mark, company, domain, likeness permissions, archive authority, or power to approve future uses.
A commercial name can identify the business presented to buyers while the image itself preserves a different maker attribution.
narrativeSequence.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · IDENTIFY — Which name is this?. Separate the person's legal name, professional name, signature, portrait, label name, house name, monogram, product line, domain, and social handle. Similar public presentation does not make these one legal object.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · LOCATE — Where is control recorded?. For a U.S. federal mark, inspect the registration and any recorded assignments; for the company, inspect governing records; for domains and accounts, inspect registrant and administrator access; for licenses and approvals, inspect executed agreements. Never substitute the label display for the record.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · DISTINGUISH — What power does each record confer?. Registration, ownership, licensed use, consent, approval, corporate voting, employment authority, account administration, and archive access answer different questions. A founder can possess some and not others.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · ESCALATE — What cannot this audit decide?. Common-law rights, state publicity law, foreign law, contractual interpretation, beneficial ownership, validity, priority, and disputed facts require jurisdiction-specific investigation and qualified counsel. The map prepares that review; it does not replace it.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: Fashion, Beauty, and Intellectual Property: Trademarks is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Government page may be cited; do not assume event media or graphics are public domain.

frames.caption: Separating the name into assets can make identity look purely transactional. A personal name also carries dignity, biography, community meaning, and reputational stakes that a registry cannot fully describe. Conversely, emotional identification with a label cannot resolve an ownership dispute. The exhibition keeps both truths visible without converting either into a legal conclusion.

Mark every unresolved common-law, publicity, contract, foreign-law, or beneficial-ownership question for counsel.
